correctness.rationale: The largest Apéry member is 4m+r, so x_r=4. For i+j=m+r the Kunz inequalities give x_i+x_j≥3, or x_i≥2 at a fixed point; these are disjoint orbits on r+1 through m−1. The only noncarry constraint with target r is i=j=1 on the second line, giving x_1≥2. Summing the disjoint lower bounds gives ceil((3m+r+1)/2), and equality forces precisely the indicated independent binary choices and fixed coordinates. Conversely every other target coordinate is ≤2, so positivity suffices there, while the constraints targeting 4 are satisfied by construction. The required largest Apéry member follows from the other coordinates being ≤2. The empty pair sets at the smallest admissible m work as well. The usual F-reflection bound with equality exactly in the symmetric/pseudosymmetric cases identifies these with all irreducibles. An independent exhaustive Kunz-vector search through m=11 found the full minimizer sets, not just the counts, in all 19 cases; it is bounded corroboration of the symbolic argument.
